approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would create new offences and penalties to stop employers exploiting temporary migrant workers.
It would let the minister prohibit an employer from hiring more temporary migrants when a court finds the employer broke migration, workplace or slavery laws.
The bill also requires the minister to publish the names of employers subject to such a prohibition and raises maximum penalties for work-related breaches.
Creates new criminal offences and civil penalties for unduly influencing, pressuring or coercing a temporary migrant worker to breach a visa condition or accept exploitative work.
Introduces a mechanism to prohibit an employer found by a court to have contravened the Migration Act, Fair Work Act or Criminal Code from hiring more temporary non-citizens.
Allows the minister to publish names of prohibited employers.
Creates a new offence for hiring a temporary migrant worker while subject to a prohibition.
Increases and aligns maximum penalties for work-related and sponsorship breaches.
Repeals section 235 of the Migration Act to avoid unintended consequences for workers.
Temporary migrant workers, their employers and labour hire intermediaries.
